Raw genomic VCF files from DNA sequencing contain hundreds of uninterpreted variants, creating a severe bottleneck where clinicians spend hours manually searching databases to evaluate patient risk. To solve this, we built an auditable, human-in-the-loop decision-support platform that transforms raw genomic data into physician-ready reports without risking AI hallucinations.

Our pipeline parses VCF files to isolate high-risk variants, then executes live API queries to MyVariant.info and NCBI PubMed to retrieve real-time annotations and literature abstracts. A Gemini RAG engine synthesizes these findings into structured reports anchored by mandatory inline citations ([ClinVar: ID], [PMID: ID]).

Governed by a LangGraph state machine, the system enforces an interrupt state where drafts are held for clinician review and revised via a feedback loop prior to sign-off. The entire workflow is traced via Langfuse for enterprise transparency.

TripWire: a zero-shot visual anomaly sentinel for physical infrastructure. Point a fixed camera at any real physical setup (a server, a cable run, a rack of hardware) and TripWire learns “normal” from a brief live calibration, no labeled data required. From there, it localizes any physical deviation in real time with a live AR heatmap showing exactly where something changed, while an on-device reasoning layer explains what changed and why it matters in plain language instead of a generic alert. The moment an anomaly is confirmed, TripWire autonomously triggers an action — no human intervention — and speaks the alert aloud. The demo: judges walk up mid-pitch and physically mess with the setup: unplug something, move something, or plant something and watch TripWire catch it, explain it, and act on it in real time, live, with nothing pre-scripted.

GreenQueue — a carbon-aware scheduler for AI compute jobs.

Right now, most systems run AI training/inference jobs the moment they're queued, even though electricity isn't equally clean all the time. GreenQueue delays non-urgent jobs to run when the power grid is cleanest (using live carbon-intensity data), while urgent jobs still run instantly.
